title: Have Gun, Will Travel
paragraphs: The radio version of the Western follows Paladin, a sophisticated San Francisco-based gunfighter who hires out his skills but often relies on judgment and negotiation as much as a weapon.
CBS radio Western adapted from the earlier television property, starring John Dehner as Paladin. Frozen GRH snapshot contains the complete numbered 1-106 radio run.

GRH documents the program through TV-script adaptation era (November 23, 1958 to August 16, 1959) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Original radio-plot era (August 23, 1959 to November 27, 1960) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]] (performer on 91 recordings), Herb Meadow (creator on 90 recordings, writer on 2 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Sam Rolfe (creator on 90 recordings and writer on 6 recordings), Ben Wright (performer on 89 recordings), Hugh Douglas (announcer on 88 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Bill James (sound-effects artist on 88 recordings), and Tom Hanley (sound-effects artist on 82 recordings, writer on 7 recordings, performer on 4 recordings, and radio adaptor on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include justice and moral judgment, hired gun and professional assignment, outlaws and violent crime, ranches and frontier property, Native American frontier conflict, and railroads and stage travel.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Television-to-radio adaptation, Late network radio drama, and Adult Western storytelling.
